candidates.requirement: Exercise parse_ex number continuation across calls on one tokener, including reconstruction of a saved exponent and rejection of a misplaced following minus sign.
candidates.target_route: Create a tokener; call parse_ex with an initial partial number, then call parse_ex again on that same tokener with the continuation.
candidates.failure_condition: The entry makes exactly one parse_ex call, then frees the tokener. A finite witness is chunks "[0e+" and "-]": the second call reaches saved exponent reconstruction and the invalid-minus guard.
candidates.alternative_paths: A single complete input can exercise ordinary exponent or minus parsing, but cannot supply saved state from an earlier call; no other call sequence exists in the complete entry.

candidates.requirement: Reach the supported strict-mode response to an incomplete exponent in parse_ex.
candidates.target_route: Set JSON_TOKENER_STRICT on the tokener, then parse a finite input such as "[0e]".
candidates.failure_condition: The target never sets flags; its default tokener remains non-strict, so the incomplete exponent is trimmed and accepted instead of taking the strict rejection route.
candidates.alternative_paths: Changing only input bytes cannot enable JSON_TOKENER_STRICT. The complete entry has no flag-setting or equivalent strict parse route.
